measures.questionText: Shall an act, passed at the 2026 session of the General Assembly, entitled “An Act authorizing the City of Cranston to finance the repair, construction, and rehabilitation of storm drains and drainage improvements, and the remediation and mitigation of drainage and flooding problems, by the issuance of not more than $4,000,000 general obligation bonds and notes therefor” be approved?
measures.officialStatement:
Explanation and purpose of Question 6: These bonds will be used to finance the repair, construction, and rehabilitation of storm drains and drainage improvements, and the remediation and mitigation of drainage and flooding problems in the city. Additionally, funds will be used to purchase equipment and resources to clean catch basins, as well as other water quality structures, as mandated by the RI DEM Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) General Permit. The goal of the program is to reduce the quantity of pollutants that enter storm sewer systems during storm events.
$4,000,000 will be borrowed. The repair, construction, and rehabilitation of storm drains and drainage improvements may begin in 2027 and may be completed in approximately 10 years. Although each asset has a different useful life, the average useful life of the drainage improvements is approximately 40 years.

Explanation and purpose of Question 7: These bonds will be used to finance acquisition, demolition, construction, improvement, renovation, repair, alteration, furnishing, and equipping of public buildings in the city, including, but not limited to, needed upgrades, repairs, and renovations to city facilities including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning and related equipment necessary to complete those upgrades. Improvements may include funding for roof repairs and/or replacements at public safety facilities (including Fire Stations 1, 2, and 3), and roof replacement at the Budlong Aquatic Center.
$2,000,000 will be borrowed. Construction and renovations on public buildings may begin in 2027 and may be completed in approximately 4 years. Although each asset has a different useful life, the average useful life of the public building improvements financed will be approximately 20 years. The useful life of the public buildings is at least 50 years. The useful life of furnishings and equipment is approximately 20 years.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cranston to borrow up to $4 million to repair, build, and rehabilitate storm drains and drainage improvements and address drainage and flooding problems. The city also plans catch-basin cleaning equipment and resources for other water-quality structures. The guide estimates $3.95 million for projects and $50,000 for issuing the debt; work may start in 2027 and take about 10 years. Assuming a 4% interest rate and level payments over 20 years, the guide estimates $1,885,000 in interest and $5,885,000 in total principal and interest. Approval grants borrowing authority; issuing bonds and spending the proceeds would still require further city action, including action by the mayor and City Council.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve borrowing authority of up to $4,000,000 for these storm drainage improvements projects, with later city action required to issue bonds and spend the money.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed borrowing authority for storm drainage improvements.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cranston to borrow up to $2 million to acquire, demolish, build, improve, renovate, repair, alter, furnish, and equip public buildings. Possible projects include heating and cooling upgrades, roof work at Fire Stations 1, 2, and 3, and replacement of the Budlong Aquatic Center roof. The guide estimates $1.96 million for projects and $40,000 for issuing the debt; work may start in 2027 and take about 4 years. Assuming a 4% interest rate and level payments over 20 years, the guide estimates $939,800 in interest and $2,939,800 in total principal and interest. Approval grants borrowing authority; issuing bonds and spending the proceeds would still require further city action, including action by the mayor and City Council.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve borrowing authority of up to $2,000,000 for these public buildings projects, with later city action required to issue bonds and spend the money.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed borrowing authority for public buildings.

Possible projects include athletic-field maintenance equipment and synthetic-turf replacement at Cranston Stadium and Cranston West. The guide estimates $3.95 million for projects and $50,000 for issuing the debt; work may start in 2027 and take about 4 years. Approval grants borrowing authority; issuing bonds and spending the proceeds would still require further city action, including action by the mayor and City Council.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve borrowing authority of up to $4,000,000 for these playgrounds and athletic fields projects, with later city action required to issue bonds and spend the money.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed borrowing authority for playgrounds and athletic fields.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cranston to borrow up to $8 million to design, build, repair, rehabilitate, and improve streets, sidewalks, and bridges, including paving, drainage, traffic controls, road-maintenance equipment, safety work, landscaping, and related costs. Possible projects include Dyer Avenue/Park Avenue intersection work; a Hope Road–Wilbur Road–Phenix Avenue roundabout; Park Avenue beautification; traffic-signal upgrades; Kimberly Lane and Phenix Avenue bridge work; Dean Street shoring; and city-road resurfacing. The guide estimates $7.94 million for projects and $60,000 for issuing the debt; work may start in 2027 and take about 4 years. Assuming a 4% interest rate and level payments over 20 years, the guide estimates $3,773,800 in interest and $11,773,800 in total principal and interest. Approval grants borrowing authority; issuing bonds and spending the proceeds would still require further city action, including action by the mayor and City Council.

measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed borrowing authority for streets, sidewalks, and bridges.

Possible projects include fire apparatus, technology, public safety equipment, training and facilities, structural repairs to 3 fire stations, and replacement of old fire apparatus and breathing equipment. The guide estimates $7.94 million for projects and $60,000 for issuing the debt; work may start in 2027 and take about 5 years. Assuming a 4% interest rate and level payments over 20 years, the guide estimates $3,773,800 in interest and $11,773,800 in total principal and interest. Approval grants borrowing authority; issuing bonds and spending the proceeds would still require further city action, including action by the mayor and City Council.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Cranston to borrow up to $25 million to buy land or buildings and build, renovate, improve, alter, repair, landscape, furnish, or equip schools and school facilities. Possible projects include boilers, roofs, heating systems, or their controls at Cranston West, Bain Middle School, Hope Highlands Middle School, Park View Middle School, and Edgewood Highland Elementary School. The guide estimates $24.9 million for projects and $100,000 for issuing the debt; work may start in 2027 and take about 3 years. For eligible projects, the city anticipates state debt-service reimbursements of up to about 53.2% of project costs. Assuming a 4% interest rate and level payments over 20 years, the guide estimates $11,789,800 in interest and $36,789,800 in total principal and interest. Approval grants borrowing authority; issuing bonds and spending the proceeds would still require further city action, including action by the mayor and City Council.

measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed borrowing authority for schools and school facilities.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the Chariho Regional School District to borrow up to $116 million to build, furnish, and equip an elementary school serving Charlestown, Richmond, and Hopkinton on one campus with one or more buildings, and improve the Switch Road Campus. Eligible costs include land, demolition, design, health and safety projects, playgrounds, landscaping, paving, and related expenses. The schools must meet Northeast Collaborative for High Performance Schools standards. Bonds may be issued only if state housing aid covers at least 61% of eligible debt service at issuance; the state share may rise to 65% at completion. The district estimates work from 2027 through about 2032. Assuming a 4.65% interest rate and debt service over 30 years, its example estimates $230,360,611 in principal and interest before state aid, $89,840,638 after 61% reimbursement, or $80,626,214 after 65% reimbursement. These are estimates; the higher state share depends on meeting the applicable requirements.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve up to $116 million in borrowing for the school campus and Switch Road improvements, subject to the minimum 61% state-aid condition.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed borrowing authority for the school campus and Switch Road improvements.
